title: Logarithmic scaling correction in quench dynamics of the J1-J2 Potts model
abstract: In conventional quench dynamics governed by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM), the defect density generally decays as a pure power law of the quench rate. However, the KZM scaling of the two-dimensional (2D) XY model with topological phase transitions features prominent logarithmic corrections. Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether such logarithmic scaling corrections emerge in discrete-spin systems that host two successive topological phase transitions under thermal quenches. This work investigates the J1-J2 antiferromagnetic Potts model and constructs its equilibrium phase diagram. Based on the temperature ranges of the paramagnetic phase, quasi-long-range ordered (QLRO) phase, long-range ordered phase, and zero-temperature ground state, we design four quench protocols with distinct temperature intervals. Our results demonstrate that quenches terminating in the QLRO phase exhibit logarithmically corrected KZM scaling of the excess energy density, consistent with the dynamical universality class of the 2D XY model. In contrast, quenches ending in the LRO phase, including both finite-temperature and zero-temperature protocols, follow conventional power-law scaling. Our results clearly uncover the characteristic scaling corrections of the J1-J2 Potts model and offer theoretical guidance for future experimental investigations of KZM via photonic simulation platforms.
summary: This paper investigates the non-equilibrium quench dynamics of the J1-J2 Potts model to determine if topological phase transitions induce logarithmic scaling corrections. Using Monte Carlo simulations across various quench protocols, the authors show that these characteristic logarithmic corrections appear only when quenching into a Quasi-Long-Range Ordered (QLRO) phase, while other quenches follow standard power-law decay.
main_problem: The study investigates whether logarithmic scaling corrections, characteristic of 2D XY models undergoing topological phase transitions, appear in discrete-spin systems exhibiting successive topological phase transitions during thermal quenches.
main_result: Quench dynamics into the Quasi-Long-Range Ordered (QLRO) phase exhibit logarithmically corrected Kibble-Zurek Mechanism scaling for excess energy density, while quenches into the Long-Range Ordered (LRO) phase follow conventional power-law scaling.
method: The authors employ Monte Carlo simulations to analyze non-equilibrium quench dynamics and construct the equilibrium phase diagram of the model.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is the J1-J2 antiferromagnetic Potts model defined on a 2D square lattice, characterized by nearest-neighbor ($J_1$) and next-nearest-neighbor ($J_2$) interactions. The model exhibits four distinct thermodynamic phases: Paramagnetic (PM), QLRO, LRO, and zero-temperature ground state.
key_observables: Excess energy density ($\delta E(t)$) and squared staggered magnetization ($\langle M_{s}^2(t)angle$).
important_parameters: The quench protocols are defined by the initial and final phases (e.g., PM $	o$ QLRO vs. PM $	o$ LRO), as well as the quench rate.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing scaling behaviors across different quench endpoints, assuming that the observed deviations from pure power laws are due to underlying topological physics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram showing PM, QLRO, and LRO regions; time evolution plots of $\delta E(t)$ and $\langle M_{s}^2(t)angle$ for various quench protocols; and log-log plots comparing scaling exponents for different regimes.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and its four phases. It then designs multiple quench protocols connecting these phases. The core of the work involves analyzing the scaling behavior of key observables ($\delta E(t)$) under these quenches, contrasting logarithmic corrections (QLRO endpoint) with pure power-law scaling (LRO endpoint).
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical test case for extending concepts from continuous symmetry models (like 2D XY model BKT transition) to discrete spin systems, which is highly relevant for understanding critical dynamics in complex quantum materials.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic illustration of the KZM. The reaction time τeq and the transition time τt are plotted as functions of the dimensionless distance t from the critical point. The intersection points of these two curves, marked by light orange circles and light green triangles at −ˆt and ˆt respectively, define the crossover between the adiabatic and impulsive regimes of the time evolution.

Figure 2. Lattice and spin basis setup for the J1–J2 three- state Potts model studied in this work. (a) Two types of pairwise spin interactions on the square lattice: gray dashed bonds are NN couplings J1 = −2, while red bonds corre- spond to NNN interactions J2 = 1. Labels A and B mark the two sublattices of the bipartite square lattice. (b) Three unit vectors ⃗θ1,2,3 forming the basis of the three-state Potts spin space. (c)–(e) Three of the six degenerate ground-state con- figurations of the model. The remaining three are obtained by exchanging two Potts spin states.

Figure 4. (a) Phase diagram of the J1–J2 Potts model, show- ing the PM, QLRO, and LRO phases separated by critical temperatures Tc1 and Tc2. (b)–(e) Four distinct quenching protocols, where the start and end points of the quenching paths are indicated by pink, yellow, red, and blue arrows, re- spectively.

Figure 3. (a) Specific heat CV versus temperature for different lattice sizes. (c) Magnetic susceptibility χ versus temperature for different lattice sizes. Vertical dotted lines mark the two thermodynamic-limit BKT critical temperatures. (b) Finite- size scaling of the high-temperature critical point Tc2 fitted via Eq. (18). (d) Finite-size scaling of the low-temperature critical point Tc1 fitted via Eq. (17).

The blue open circles denote the peak posi- tions at t = ˆtH corresponding to the high-temperature critical point Tc2 whereas the magenta open circles indicate the ter- mination time t = 2τQ of each quench inside the QLRO phase at T = 1.5.
